title: garage: main light with two switches in parallel and an emergency light with its own battery, fuse and test button
style: Normal, clear but not exhaustive; if the agent asks something, answer exactly that.
facts: It is your garage. THERE ARE TWO SOURCES OF CURRENT: the garage mains (garage_mains) and an emergency battery (backup_battery). From garage_mains runs a main wire (garage_wire). From garage_wire two wires leave, door_wire and back_wire, each controlled by its own switch: door_sw (next to the door) controls door_wire and back_sw (at the back) controls back_wire; each switch closes its wire when it is up. Both wires, door_wire and back_wire, go to the same main light (garage_light): it is enough for ONE of the two switches to be up for it to be lit (they are in parallel). EMERGENCY LIGHT (em_light): it gets current from a wire em_wire. em_wire gets current from backup_battery through the fuse em_fuse (if em_fuse is in good condition), and ALSO from garage_wire through a test button test_sw (when test_sw is up). STATE AT THE START: door_sw down, back_sw down, test_sw down, fuse em_fuse and lamps in good condition. EVENTS, in this order: 1) you raise door_sw; 2) you raise back_sw; 3) you lower door_sw; 4) you lower back_sw; 5) em_fuse blows; 6) you raise test_sw.
questions: Which lamps are lit at the start?
Why is garage_light not lit at the start?
Why is garage_light lit after event 3 (when you have already lowered door_sw)?
Why is em_light not lit after event 5?
Why did garage_light change over the course of all the events?
EXTENSION: tell it that after all that (event 7) you lower test_sw, and ask why em_light is not lit at the end.
